title: A3C-Based Dynamic Stock Portfolio Construction Using KOSPI 200 Constituents
content: Equity-market trading systems must account for constraints such as integer-share trading, transaction fees, and taxes. This study proposes a reinforcement learning–based trading system (RLTS) for dynamic portfolio construction and trading in the Korean stock market. Daily price data for stocks included in the Korea Composite Stock Price Index 200 (KOSPI 200) from 2011 to 2021 were used to generate technical-indicator inputs. An asynchronous advantage actor–critic (A3C) algorithm was used to train a shared network across stocks, and stocks whose training-period returns exceeded the risk-free rate were selected as portfolio constituents. Portfolios constructed using 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-month training windows were evaluated during subsequent testing periods and compared with portfolios generated using deep Q-network (DQN) and policy-gradient (PG) algorithms. The A3C-based portfolios achieved positive average returns and Sharpe ratios for all training-window widths, with the 9-month window producing the highest average return (11.43%) and Sharpe ratio (6.40). Two-way analysis of variance identified significant main effects of the RL algorithm and training-window width, but no significant interaction. These findings indicate that A3C outperformed DQN and PG under the tested conditions and that training-window selection influenced portfolio performance.
